_comment: The analysis model weights: what they are, where they come from, and how to know a copy is
intact. Read by build/fetchModels.mjs (the developer's copy) and by the Electron main process
(the listener's download), so the two cannot disagree about which file is the right file.
The hash is the point of this file, not the URLs. 'Downloaded successfully' and 'usable' are
different claims, and four separate times in this project a publisher's weights arrived intact
and still would not load. A truncated or mirror-substituted ONNX does not fail loudly - it
loads and answers confidently and wrongly, which for a beat grid means every transition lands
off the beat with nothing in the log to say why. That risk goes UP once the file can come from
a mirror, a netdisk, or a folder the listener pointed us at.
Mirrors are tried in order and the first one whose bytes match the hash wins. hf-mirror is
first because it is the only route reachable from mainland China, which is where most of
Folia's listeners are; it serves everyone else too, so this is not a special case, it is the
order that works for the most people. The GitHub release is our own mirror of last resort.
Both models are MIT, which is what makes hosting our own copies allowed at all. A CC-BY-NC
model could never be listed here while Folia is AGPL-3.0 - see the licence field.
The third entry is not a model - it is the Python the model runs in, and it is the one entry
with a `platforms` block because there is a different archive per OS. A platform missing from
that block cannot run separation at all, and is reported as unsupported rather than offered a
download. darwin-x64 is in it with an older onnxruntime than the rest (see buildPythonRuntime.mjs);
it could not be until build/htdemucs_cut_fft.py took the DFTs out of the model.
_manualComment: Shown only when every mirror has failed. An empty list = the settings page does not offer the
manual route at all, which is right: an empty link is worse than no link. Adding a route is a
data change with no code edit, which is the point of it living here.
Two netdisks rather than one because the failure they cover is regional and account-shaped:
Baidu throttles or demands a client, Quark does not, and which of the two a given listener can
actually use is not something we can know from here. Each carries its own extraction code, so
the code belongs to the link and not to the block.
The manual route ends at the same place the automatic one does - a file in the models
directory - so what the app does with a netdisk download is verify it and copy it in, exactly
what it does with a downloaded one. There is no second trust level for files a human carried.

models.name: beat_this
models.note: Beat This! (CPJKU, ISMIR 2024), the community ONNX export of the authors' own final0 checkpoint.

models.name: htdemucs
models.note: htdemucs (Meta Research), single-file four-stem variant, fp16 weights, and the upstream repo's 'transparent' re-export, which makes the STFT a real DFT operator instead of an unrolled loop, taking the graph from 24917 nodes to 1556, so ORT's optimizer costs 353MB and 0.65s where the ordinary export cost 4594MB and 3.9s. Two edits are ours, on top of that. First, build/htdemucs_halve_segment.py halves the welded-in segment, 343980 to 172032 samples (7.8s to 3.9s): peak working set 789MB to 483MB and 19% FASTER, because attention is quadratic in the token count and the segment sets it. A blind A/B on four rendered transitions could not separate the two segment lengths. Second, build/htdemucs_cut_fft.py takes the STFT's and iSTFT's DFTs out of the graph and htdemucs_runner.py does them in numpy: onnxruntime before 1.25, the only kind with an Intel Mac wheel, cannot load the iSTFT's inverse one-sided DFT, and numpy's real FFT is faster anyway (4.9s to 4.2s per 30s window on onnxruntime 1.29), the stems differing by float rounding (123 dB SNR). A new file name rather than a new htdemucs.onnx, because an app from before cannot run it: overwriting the old name would have failed their downloads on the hash. The old file still resolves as installed (modelPaths.cjs MODEL_FILES).

models.name: runtime
models.note: CPython 3.11.16 + onnxruntime 1.29.0 (1.23.2 on Intel Macs, the last with a wheel for them, which needs macOS 13) + numpy 2.4.6, built by build/buildPythonRuntime.mjs. Separation runs here rather than in Electron's own onnxruntime-node because `enable_mem_reuse` is bound only by onnxruntime's Python API, and turning it off is what takes one separation from 2543MB to under 500MB. A directory rather than a file: it is unpacked into <models>/runtime/ and the interpreter is <models>/runtime/python.exe, or bin/python3 off Windows.
